name: Bar too far from shins at setup
looks_like: Visible gap between bar and shins before lift-off; bar sits over toes instead of over the balls of the feet.
downstream: Bar swings out off the floor
signal: At lift-off frame: horizontal distance from plate centre to ankle keypoint, scaled by plate diameter (45 cm bumper = known length). Compare to the lifter's own rep history rather than an absolute norm.

threshold.value: plate centre > 20 cm in front of ankle keypoint at lift-off
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); bar-over-balls-of-feet guidance from CrossFit L1

cues: Bar over the balls of your feet
Shins touch the bar before you pull
Roll the bar in to your shins
Knees over the bar at the start
Pull the bar in before it leaves
Start with the bar brushing your laces
why: If the bar starts away from you, it has to swing back in or you have to chase it forward.

name: Hips too high at setup
looks_like: Start looks like a stiff-leg deadlift: knees nearly straight, torso close to horizontal, shoulders far in front of the bar.
root_causes: Weak quads at deep knee angles
signal: At lift-off: knee angle (hip-knee-ankle) and torso angle from horizontal (hip-shoulder line).

threshold.value: knee angle > 115 deg AND torso < 20 deg above horizontal at lift-off
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified)

cues: Sit the hips down to start
Chest up before the bar moves
Push the floor away with your legs
Start like a jump, not a deadlift
why: Your legs are the strongest engine off the floor. Hips too high take them out of the lift.

name: Hips too low / squatting the bar up
looks_like: Start looks like a squat: hips at or below knees, torso very upright, shoulders behind the bar; hips then shoot up as the bar breaks.
downstream: Hips shoot up anyway once the bar moves
Knees in the way of the bar
Bar swings out around the knees
signal: At lift-off: hip keypoint height vs knee keypoint height; shoulder x relative to plate centre x.

threshold.value: hip at or below knee height (within 5 cm) at lift-off
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); CF L1: hips higher than knees, lower than shoulders

cues: Hips a little higher than knees
Do not squat the bar off
Arms hang straight down to the bar
why: A start that is too low just turns into hips-shooting-up once the bar gets heavy.
drills: Pause at the knee snatch deadlift

name: Shoulders behind the bar at start
looks_like: From the side the shoulder joint is behind the bar line at lift-off.
downstream: Bar swings out as it leaves the floor
signal: Shoulder keypoint x minus plate centre x at lift-off (sign by lifter facing direction).

threshold.value: shoulder > 5 cm behind plate centre at lift-off
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); Kauhanen 1984 (via Cissik): elite shoulders further in front of bar at start

cues: Shoulders over or just ahead of bar
Lean over the bar a little
Cover the bar with your shoulders
why: Shoulders slightly over the bar lets the bar move back toward you, not away.

name: Rounded back at setup or off the floor
looks_like: Lumbar or thoracic spine flexes before or as the bar breaks.
signal: 2D keypoints (hip, shoulder) give a straight segment; spine curvature is not recoverable at ~5 cm error. Would need a dedicated back-contour model.

threshold.value: none found
threshold.source: none found

cues: Show your logo to the front
why: A soft back bends under load and steals the force your legs make.

name: Hips shoot up off the floor
looks_like: Right after lift-off the hips rise quickly while the bar and shoulders barely move; torso tips toward horizontal.
root_causes: Yanking the bar off the floor without tension
Legs weak at small knee angles relative to hips
signal: Floor-to-knee window: (a) change in torso angle (hip-shoulder line vs horizontal) from lift-off to bar at knee height; (b) hip vertical rise vs plate vertical rise over the first ~150 ms. Both use segments of ~50 cm so 5 cm joint error is ~6 deg.

threshold.value: torso angle drops > 15 deg between lift-off and bar at knee, OR hip rises > 2x plate rise in first 150 ms
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); qualitative definition from Everett (Catalyst) and CF L1 ('hips and shoulders rise at the same rate')

cues: Lift the chest with your legs
Squeeze the bar off the floor
Keep your back angle until the knee
Slow off the floor, fast at the top
why: If your hips rise first, your back does the work and the bar drifts forward.
Bar speed is what counts, not hip speed.
drills: Pause snatch deadlift (just off floor and at knee)

name: Rushing / jerking the bar off the floor
looks_like: Bar snaps off the floor with a spike in speed, often with a visible bounce of the plates or hips rising first.
root_causes: Thinking a fast first pull is better
No pre-tension in the arms and back
downstream: Second pull from a bad position
signal: Plate vertical velocity: peak velocity in floor-to-knee phase relative to peak velocity in second pull. Elite: ~1.00 m/s first vs ~1.93 m/s second (ratio ~0.5).

threshold.value: first-pull peak / second-pull peak bar velocity > 0.7
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); elite reference values from Nagao 2019 (1.00 vs 1.93 m/s) and Harbili 2014 (0.98 vs 1.82 m/s)

cues: Squeeze it off, don't rip it
Build speed as the bar rises
Smooth to the knee, violent at the hip
why: The bar should keep speeding up. Ripping it off the floor wrecks the position you need for the jump.

name: Bar drifts away in the first pull
looks_like: Bar moves forward, away from the shins, between floor and knee; a gap opens at knee height.
signal: Plate-centre horizontal displacement from lift-off to the frame the bar passes knee height (plate tracking is ~1-2 cm, scaled by plate diameter). Elite bars move toward the lifter in the first pull.

threshold.value: net horizontal move away from lifter > 2 cm by knee height
threshold.source: Elite first-pull displacement toward lifter: 6 +/- 3 cm (Harbili 2014), 7 +/- 3 cm (Nagao 2019 Dx1), 3-9 cm (Garhammer 1985 via Petrizzo 2016); cutoff itself is heuristic, not from a source (unverified)

cues: Keep the bar on your legs
Sweep the bar back to you
Pull the bar into your shins
Bar brushes all the way up
why: A bar that drifts away is heavier and has to be pulled back or chased.
Every cm forward is a cm you must fix later.

name: Bar moves straight up past the knees (no sweep back)
looks_like: Bar rises vertically or slightly forward past the knees instead of moving slightly back toward the thighs.
root_causes: Not shifting balance back as the bar leaves
downstream: Bar meets the thighs too far forward
Bar swings out in the second pull
signal: Plate-centre horizontal displacement from lift-off to bar at mid-thigh (knee-height + ~15 cm).

threshold.value: toward-lifter displacement < 2 cm by mid-thigh
threshold.source: Everett (Catalyst) cause #4 of jumping forward; elite toward-lifter 3-9 cm (Garhammer via Petrizzo), 6 cm (Harbili); cutoff heuristic, not from a source (unverified)

cues: Bar travels back past the knees
Sweep the bar into your thighs
Shift to midfoot as it breaks
why: A small sweep back lines the bar up with your hips so the jump drives it up, not out.

name: Early arm bend
looks_like: Elbows bend before the hips and knees finish extending; bar is pulled with the arms off the thighs.
root_causes: Grip too narrow (bar lands low on thigh)
Starting the second pull too early
downstream: Lost power from legs and hips
Elbows go back, not up and out
signal: Elbow angle (shoulder-elbow-wrist) of the near-side arm, tracked from lift-off until max hip extension. Forearm/upper arm segments ~30 cm so 5 cm error is ~10 deg; use a large margin. Wrist may be occluded by plate; use bar centre as the wrist proxy.

threshold.value: elbow angle < 150 deg before peak hip/knee extension
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified) (margin for 10 deg error); fault definition from CF L1/L3 and Everett

cues: Arms are ropes, legs are the engine
When the arms bend, the power ends
Finish the legs before the arms
why: Bent arms soak up the force your legs make instead of passing it to the bar.
drills: Hang power snatch with straight-arm focus

name: Shoulders behind the bar too early
looks_like: Torso becomes upright or leans back before the bar reaches mid-thigh; shoulders move behind the bar early.
root_causes: Fear of being on the toes
downstream: Bar contacts low on the thigh
signal: Shoulder x relative to plate-centre x and torso angle vs vertical while the plate is below mid-thigh.

threshold.value: shoulder behind plate centre while bar below mid-thigh, OR torso within 20 deg of vertical before bar at mid-thigh
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); Everett: stay over the bar until mid/upper thigh; Kauhanen: elite shoulders behind bar only by the explosive phase

cues: Shoulders over the bar to mid-thigh
Wait for the bar to reach your hips
Chest over the bar, then jump
why: Opening early wastes the hips. Wait until the bar is high on your thigh, then jump.

name: Starting the jump too low
looks_like: The explosive hip drive begins with the bar at or just above the knee instead of mid/upper thigh.
signal: Bar height at the onset of the second-pull acceleration (where plate vertical velocity starts its main rise) relative to the knee keypoint height measured at that frame.

threshold.value: acceleration onset with plate < 10 cm above knee height
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); CrossFit coach: second pull started at/above knees causes forward drift

cues: Jump from the hips, not the knees
Wait until the bar is high
Bar to the pockets, then jump
why: The jump only works when the bar is near your hips.

name: Bar slows down in the transition (scoop stall)
looks_like: Bar visibly slows or stalls as it passes the knees while the knees rebend (forced scoop).
root_causes: Weak hamstrings/back in the knee position
downstream: Less bar speed into the second pull
signal: Plate vertical velocity: local minimum between first-pull peak and second-pull peak, as a fraction of the first-pull peak. Sample at >= 60 fps; smooth over 3 frames.

threshold.value: velocity dip > 30% of first-pull peak
threshold.source: Kipp & Harris 2015: heavier relative loads showed smaller acceleration drops in the second knee bend, coaches should limit deceleration; numeric cutoff heuristic, not from a source (unverified)

why: A bar that stalls at the knee needs extra effort to get going again.

name: Bar contacts low on the thigh
looks_like: Bar bangs off mid-thigh instead of brushing the hip crease/upper thigh.
signal: Height of the plate centre at its most-backward point in the second pull (contact proxy) relative to the hip keypoint height.

threshold.value: most-backward bar point > 15 cm below hip keypoint
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); Everett: in snatch the bar should sit in the hip crease at arm's length

cues: Brush the bar at your hips
Contact high, not on the thigh
why: Hitting low on the thigh kicks the bar forward instead of up.

name: Bar swings / loops forward off the hips
looks_like: After hip contact the bar arcs well out in front, often beyond the starting line; classic 'loop'.
root_causes: Hips driving forward into the bar (hip bang)
Bar away from body before contact
downstream: Lifter jumps forward to chase it
signal: Plate-centre horizontal: (a) max forward excursion from the most-backward point in second pull to max height (Nagao Dx2); (b) whether the bar crosses in front of its lift-off vertical line before the catch.

threshold.value: Dx2 > 15 cm, OR bar > 3 cm in front of start line during second pull/turnover
threshold.source: Elite reference Dx2 0.12 +/- 0.09 m (Nagao 2019); second-pull away-from-lifter 4 +/- 3 cm (Harbili 2014); 3-18 cm range (Garhammer via Petrizzo); cutoffs heuristic, not from a source (unverified)

cues: Keep the bar close to your body
Hips to the bar, not through it
Drive the floor, not the hips
why: Hitting the bar with your hips throws it away from you; then you must chase it.
A vertical push puts all your power into height.

name: Not finishing the pull (pulling under early)
looks_like: Lifter drops under before hips and knees reach full extension; no visible tall finish.
signal: Max knee angle and max torso-from-vertical during second pull; also bar peak height relative to lifter standing height (estimate from frame 0 head/ankle keypoints).

threshold.value: max knee angle < 155 deg OR torso still > 10 deg forward of vertical at peak extension
threshold.source: Elite max second-pull knee extension 165 +/- 5 deg, hip ~200 deg (Harbili 2014); cutoff includes ~10 deg error margin, heuristic, not from a source (unverified)

cues: Stand all the way up first
Hips through before you pull under
Push the floor through the top
why: The bar only goes as high as your extension sends it.
Pulling under early leaves power on the floor.

name: Leaning back too far at the top
looks_like: At the finish the torso leans far behind vertical; lifter looks like a banana.
signal: Torso angle behind vertical (hip-shoulder line) at peak hip extension.

threshold.value: torso > 30 deg behind vertical at peak extension
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); Everett: over-extending causes jump back; elite hip angle ~200 deg (Harbili) implies a modest lean back

cues: Shoulders over hips at the top
why: Leaning back spends time you need to get under the bar.

name: Feet leave the floor too soon
looks_like: Heels lift and feet start moving before the hips and knees finish extending.
signal: Ankle keypoint vertical rise (or heel keypoint if model has it) relative to time of peak knee angle.

threshold.value: ankle rise > 3 cm more than 40 ms before peak knee extension
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); Everett (premature lift of the feet)

cues: Push the floor until you finish
Heels down until the hips open
Feet quiet until you are tall
why: Your feet are your connection to the floor; lift them early and the push stops.

name: Bar does not go high enough
looks_like: Bar peaks low (around the belly) and the lifter has to catch very deep and fast or misses.
root_causes: Load too heavy for current power
signal: Peak plate-centre height / lifter standing height (lifter height from setup or a standing frame). Interpret with load: heavier loads lower the ratio.

threshold.value: peak bar height < 65% of lifter height on a squat snatch
threshold.source: Elite ~72% vs district 76% (Kauhanen 1984 via Cissik); Campos & Rabade claim < 71.9% predicts no-lift (secondary, UNVERIFIED); 65% cutoff heuristic, not from a source (unverified)

cues: Drive the bar up with your legs
Push the floor hard at the top
why: More height gives you more time to get under. Elite lifters still need only ~70% of their height.

name: Slow turnover / late getting under
looks_like: Bar reaches peak and stalls or starts falling before the lifter is locked out underneath.
root_causes: Late start to the pull under
signal: Time from peak hip/knee extension frame to the catch frame (bar vertical velocity ~0 after the drop with elbow angle > 160 deg). Needs >= 60 fps; 120-240 fps preferred.

threshold.value: turnover > 0.40 s
threshold.source: Torokhtiy: 0.25-0.30 s for pros, 0.4-0.7 s for beginners; JSSM table: 0.235 +/- 0.02 s (men and women)

why: The bar is weightless for a split second at the top. That is when you must get under it.

name: Bar crashes into the catch
looks_like: Large free fall between peak and catch; the bar slams onto locked arms and the lifter is driven down.
root_causes: Letting go of the bar in the third pull
signal: Bar drop distance Dy3 = peak plate height minus plate height at catch (plate scale). Also peak downward plate velocity before catch.

threshold.value: drop > 25 cm (squat snatch)
threshold.source: Nagao 2019: successful 0.17 +/- 0.04 m vs unsuccessful 0.18 m (p<0.001); Carlson 2001 women ~20.8 cm; cutoff heuristic, not from a source (unverified)

cues: Hold the bar the whole way
why: The less the bar falls, the softer and safer the catch.
Successful elite snatches drop less than missed ones.

name: Bar caught too far forward
looks_like: At the catch the bar is ahead of the lifter's midfoot/ahead of the starting line; lifter is pulled forward onto toes.
root_causes: Not bringing bar back in third pull
signal: Plate-centre x at catch relative to (a) plate x at lift-off and (b) ankle keypoint x. Elite successful lifts bring the bar back further (DxL).

threshold.value: catch bar ahead of start line by > 2 cm, OR DxL < 5 cm
threshold.source: Nagao 2019: DxL successful 0.11 +/- 0.05 m vs unsuccessful 0.10 m; 65.8% of elite misses were frontward drops; cutoffs heuristic, not from a source (unverified)

cues: Pull the bar back over you
Bar over the back of your neck
why: Elite lifters miss forward far more than backward; bringing the bar back over your heels saves lifts.

name: Bar caught too far behind
looks_like: Bar passes behind the head/shoulders at the catch; lifter falls back or dumps behind.
root_causes: Excess forward trunk lean in squat (poor overhead structure)
signal: Plate-centre x vs shoulder keypoint x and vs ankle keypoint at catch.

threshold.value: plate > 10 cm behind shoulder keypoint at catch
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); 25.1% of elite misses were backward (Nagao 2019)

cues: Bar over the back of your neck
Elbows up and out, not back
why: The bar only stays up if it ends over your feet.

name: Soft elbows / press-out
looks_like: Arms not locked when the bar lands; elbows then extend under load (press-out). A no-lift in competition.
signal: Near-side elbow angle at the catch frame and its change over the next ~300 ms while the bar is not rising. Near arm is visible side-on but the plate may occlude it; overhead elbow error ~10 deg.

threshold.value: elbow angle < 160 deg at catch, then increases > 10 deg
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); fault definition from CF L3 and Performance Menu; 9.1% of elite failures were press-out or quit (Nagao 2019)

cues: Lock your arms as you land
why: Bent elbows have to press the bar, and pressing is a no-lift.

name: Jumping forward
looks_like: Feet land clearly in front of where they started; lifter chases the bar forward.
root_causes: Weight on toes in first pull
Bar moving straight up past knees
Bar swinging forward in second/third pull
signal: Ankle keypoint x at catch minus ankle x at setup (average both feet if visible); compare to plate x change to see whether body and bar moved together.

threshold.value: ankle moves forward > 8 cm
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified) (margin for ~5 cm ankle error); Everett: mat a few inches in front of toes as deterrent

why: Jumping forward means the bar went forward first; fix the bar and the feet follow.
drills: Mat or tape line in front of toes

name: Jumping back away from the bar
looks_like: Feet slide back further than the bar does; lifter ends up behind the bar or with the bar pulling them forward.
root_causes: Weight too far back on heels
downstream: Bar ends in front of the base
signal: Ankle backward displacement minus plate backward displacement from setup to catch. Equal backward movement is fine (Everett rules).

threshold.value: feet move back > 8 cm more than the bar
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); Everett: OK only if body, feet and bar move back equally; elite rearward foot displacement of 10-18 cm reported and not detrimental (Schilling 2002)

cues: Plant your feet under the bar
Push the floor until you finish
Move with the bar, not away
why: A little hop back is fine if the bar comes with you. Feet running away from the bar is not.

name: Landing too wide (starfish)
looks_like: Feet land far wider than squat stance, often on inner edges.
signal: Width is a frontal-plane measure; side-on cannot see stance width. Flag only via other angle.

threshold.value: none found (side-on)
threshold.source: none found

why: Your catch stance should match your squat stance so you can stand up.

name: Catching high and riding it down
looks_like: On a squat snatch the bar is received with hips well above parallel, then lifter sinks under load.
signal: Hip keypoint height at the catch frame (elbow lock + bar velocity ~0) vs minimum hip height afterwards; also continued bar descent after catch.

threshold.value: hip descends > 15 cm after the catch frame
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); fault from CF L3

cues: Meet the bar at the bottom
Pull yourself all the way down
Lock out and sit at once
why: Catching high then sinking means you catch the bar twice.

name: Torso too far forward in the catch
looks_like: In the bottom the chest falls forward and the arms angle back to keep the bar over the feet.
signal: Torso angle from vertical (hip-shoulder line) in the bottom of the catch.

threshold.value: torso > 35 deg forward of vertical in the bottom
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); Everett: only a very slight forward lean, bar over back of neck

cues: Sit the hips down, not back
Bar over the back of the neck
why: The more upright you are, the easier the bar balances over you.

name: Diving the head and chest under
looks_like: During the pull under the head and chest move forward and down to squeeze under the bar.
signal: Shoulder keypoint horizontal shift forward from peak extension to catch, relative to plate.

threshold.value: shoulder moves > 10 cm forward relative to plate during turnover
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); Everett (missing behind)

cues: Elbows up and to the sides
why: Diving forward pushes the bar behind you.

name: Landing on the toes
looks_like: Heels off the floor at the catch, weight on the front of the foot.
signal: Heel/ankle keypoint height vs its setup height at catch (requires visible heel or ankle).

threshold.value: ankle > 3 cm above setup height at catch
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); CF L1 'landing forward on toes'

why: Flat feet give you a base to stand the bar up from.

name: Losing the bar in the recovery
looks_like: After a good catch the bar drifts forward or the hips rise first on the stand, and the bar is lost or chased.
signal: Plate horizontal travel and torso angle change from bottom of catch to standing.

threshold.value: bar travels > 8 cm horizontally during stand, OR torso leans forward > 15 deg on the stand
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified)

why: Pausing a beat in the bottom lets the bar settle before you stand.

name: Hang: bar leaves the thigh in the dip
looks_like: In hang snatch, as the lifter hinges down to the start, the bar comes off the thighs or knees push forward.
signal: Plate x relative to hip/knee keypoints during the dip; plate away from the thigh line.

threshold.value: plate moves > 5 cm forward during the dip
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified)

cues: Slide the bar down your thighs
Push the hips back in the dip
why: The hang only works if the bar stays on you during the hinge.
drills: Hang snatch from mid-thigh with pause

name: Power snatch received below parallel
looks_like: On a power snatch the lifter's hips go below the knees (it became a squat snatch).
root_causes: Load too heavy for a power
downstream: Not a power snatch; may indicate weak second pull
signal: Hip keypoint height vs knee keypoint height at the lowest point of the catch.

threshold.value: hip below knee height by > 5 cm at lowest point
threshold.source: Power definition: received above parallel; margin heuristic, not from a source (unverified)

why: A power snatch catches above parallel. Going lower means the bar was not high enough.

name: Grip too narrow or too wide
looks_like: Narrow grip: bar contacts mid-thigh, lifter bends arms. Wide grip: bar travels behind easily, unstable overhead.
signal: Width itself not visible side-on. Proxy: bar contact height vs hip keypoint when standing with arms straight at setup or end of pull.

threshold.value: bar > 10 cm below hip crease at full arm extension standing
threshold.source: heuristic, not from a source (unverified); Everett: snatch bar should sit in hip crease at arm's length

cues: Bar in the hip crease standing
Widen until the bar hits your hips
Knuckles to hip crease when standing
why: Grip width sets where the bar hits you. The hip crease is the target.
drills: Snatch push press for wide-grip stability

name: Missed forward (outcome)
looks_like: Bar is dropped in front of the lifter after reaching overhead or during the catch.
signal: Plate falls to the floor in front of the start line after reaching overhead height.

threshold.value: plate returns to floor > 10 cm in front of start x
threshold.source: Outcome detection; 65.8% of elite failed snatches were frontward (Nagao 2019)

cues: Bring the bar back over you
why: Most forward misses start in the first pull; fix the earliest fault first.

name: Missed behind (outcome)
looks_like: Bar passes behind the head and is dumped backward.
signal: Plate falls to the floor behind the lifter's ankle/start line after overhead.

threshold.value: plate returns to floor behind ankle x
threshold.source: Outcome detection; 25.1% of elite failed snatches were backward (Nagao 2019)

cues: Stop the bar over your head
why: Missing behind is often over-pulling or a grip that is too wide, not a lack of strength.
